subject: Fjord Labs - Renewal: capacity slope & commit timing proposal
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@fjordlabs.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fjord Labs - Renewal: capacity slope & commit timing proposal

Hi Samir —

Thanks for sharing the usage export last quarter. I ran our initial sizing pass and have a proposal that balances your on-demand peaks with a modest committed tranche to lower unit cost.

Summary in one line: recommend adding a 40-GPU committed tranche now, staged to 80 GPUs over 10 weeks if weekly sustained utilization > 68%.

Why this approach:
- Your 7-day p95 token latency-sensitive slices are currently triggering burst usage at predictable times; a small committed base buys headroom and lower per-token pricing.
- Staged ramp avoids a large upfront commit while giving operations runway to dry-run traffic shaping and KV caching.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I’ll attach a capacity snapshot and a draft commit schedule for procurement review.
2) If procurement is okay, we can lock pricing and schedule the tranche in 2-week increments.
3) If you want to accelerate to full 80 GPUs, we can provide a short-term burst buffer (30% overcommit) for 6 weeks.

I’ve CC’d Karthik to validate the rollout cadence and Marissa for final approval on the concession we discussed.

Attachments: capacity_snapshot_Jun2026.csv, proposed_commit_schedule_v2.pdf

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0139

From: Samir Gupta <samir@fjordlabs.ai>

Cc: procurement@fjordlabs.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:08:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Fjord Labs - Renewal: capacity slope & commit timing proposal

Tessa —

Appreciate the quick read. A few data points from our side: last 30 days, average steady usage ~32 GPUs, daily peak events push to ~95 GPUs for 2-3 hours, weekly p95 around 72 GPUs. Latency spikes matter for our customer-facing inference pipelines (real-time recommenders).

Questions:
- Does the 40 -> 80 ramp assume prefix/KV caching effectiveness at current hit rates (~45%)?
- Can you model cost for a 60-GPU committed plan versus your recommended staged ramp?
- Procurement prefers fewer line items — can we consolidate into a single 12-month staged commitment?

I’m looping procurement for the formal side. If you can get a clear cost delta and a proposed DocuSign-ready SOW, we can prioritize before our board review next month.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform, Fjord Labs

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@fjordlabs.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, procurement@fjordlabs.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:05:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Fjord Labs - Renewal: capacity slope & commit timing proposal

Samir —

Answers inline and attached a single-sheet cost comparison (see proposed_commit_schedule_v2.pdf).

- KV caching assumption: the ramp uses a conservative 50% effective cache hit for first 6 weeks, then 65% once your existing cache warms and the runtime tuning is applied. I’ve noted sensitivity in the spreadsheet.
- 60-GPU committed option: attached; it sits in the middle — 10% lower blended price vs staged ramp, but less headroom during unexpected peaks. Looking at your peaks (95 GPUs) we recommend a burst buffer of 35 GPUs for short windows if you pick the 60-GPU route.
- Single 12-month staged commitment: doable. We’ll draft a single SOW with calendarized tranche delivery (0/30/60/90 days style). Procurement can sign one SOW and we’ll track tranche activation internally.

I’ll bring Karthik in for the rollout ops timeline and Marissa for an approval on the prospect discount band.

Best,
Tessa

Attachments: proposed_commit_schedule_v2.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, procurement@fjordlabs.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 09:30:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Fjord Labs - Renewal: capacity slope & commit timing proposal

Team —

Operational notes and recommended cadence:
- Provisioning lead time for new committed GPUs is 7–10 business days for Reserved pools; burst buffer is available within 48 hours as temporary capacity.
- Rollout cadence we recommend for the single-SOW (12 months) option: activate 40 GPUs at contract execution, 20 GPUs at week 4, final 20 GPUs at week 10. That gives you 80 GPUs committed by week 10 while reducing initial cost.
- Canary ops: we’ll enable prefix caching and KV warmup on a canary subset (10% of traffic) for 7 days before each tranche activation. Observability hooks: token-level cost, model latency, and a rollback path to reduce tranche activation by pausing scheduled allocation.

Procurement considerations: attach SOW draft in next mail. For discount banding: we can offer a 5% unit discount if Fjord signs a 12-month single-SOW and commits to a minimum average utilization of 55% across the first 90 days.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
